# Screening & Unscreening in Mo 3d Spectra

Good question. Let me clarify what you're observing:

## What Are Screened vs. Unscreened Peaks?

In **transition metal oxides**, particularly Mo 3d, you can have:

• **Unscreened (main) peaks** — the primary 3d photohole is not screened by valence electrons. These are the dominant features and represent the "true" oxidation state.

• **Screened peaks** — the 3d photohole is screened by a valence electron (e.g., 3d⁵L̄ configuration, where L̄ is a ligand hole). These appear at **lower binding energy** (~1–3 eV below the main peak) and are typically **weaker** (10–30% of main peak intensity).

## Your Current Fit (8 peaks)

Your fit shows **4 oxidation states** (Mo⁰, MoO₂, Mo⁵⁺, MoO₃), each with a 3d5/2 and 3d3/2 doublet. This is a **main-peak-only model** — no screening satellites are included.

**Is this correct for your sample?**

For **sputtered Mo-Ni-Ox**, screening satellites are often **weak or absent** because:
- Sputtering can create defects and disorder that suppress screening
- The sample may be partially reduced (Mo⁰ present), which has no screening
- Oxide screening satellites are typically only prominent in well-crystallised, stoichiometric oxides

## Should You Add Screening Satellites?

**Check your raw spectrum:**
- Look for **small shoulders or bumps 1–3 eV below each main peak** (lower BE side)
- If present and visible above noise, add screened components
- If absent or negligible, your current 8-peak model is appropriate

**If you want to add screening satellites**, the structure would be:

• **Mo⁰ screened** — ~1.5–2 eV below Mo⁰ main (very weak, often absent in sputtered samples)
• **MoO₂ screened** — ~1–2 eV below MoO₂ main
• **Mo⁵⁺ screened** — ~1–2 eV below Mo⁵⁺ main
• **MoO₃ screened** — ~1–2 eV below MoO₃ main (most prominent screening in fully oxidised state)

---

## Recommendation

**Before adding screening satellites, answer:**

1. Do you see distinct shoulders or secondary peaks 1–3 eV **lower** (left) of your main peaks in the raw data?
2. Is the fit residual currently acceptable, or are there systematic deviations?

If **yes to (1)** or **poor residual**, I can help you add screened components with proper labelling:


# Screening & Unscreening in Mo 3d Spectra

Good question. Let me clarify what you're observing:

## What Are Screened vs. Unscreened Peaks?

In **transition metal oxides**, particularly Mo 3d, you can have:

• **Unscreened (main) peaks** — the primary 3d photohole is not screened by valence electrons. These are the dominant features and represent the "true" oxidation state.

• **Screened peaks** — the 3d photohole is screened by a valence electron (e.g., 3d⁵L̄ configuration, where L̄ is a ligand hole). These appear at **lower binding energy** (~1–3 eV below the main peak) and are typically **weaker** (10–30% of main peak intensity).

For **sputtered Mo-Ni-Ox**, screening satellites are often **weak or absent** because:
- Sputtering can create defects and disorder that suppress screening
- The sample may be partially reduced (Mo⁰ present), which has no screening
- Oxide screening satellites are typically only prominent in well-crystallised, stoichiometric oxides

**Check your raw spectrum:**
- Look for **small shoulders or bumps 1–3 eV below each main peak** (lower BE side)

Screening & Unscreening in Mo 3d Spectra
Good question. Let me clarify what you're observing:

What Are Screened vs. Unscreened Peaks?
In transition metal oxides, particularly Mo 3d, you can have:

• Unscreened (main) peaks — the primary 3d photohole is not screened by valence electrons. These are the dominant features and represent the "true" oxidation state.

• Screened peaks — the 3d photohole is screened by a valence electron (e.g., 3d⁵L̄ configuration, where L̄ is a ligand hole). These appear at lower binding energy (~1–3 eV below the main peak) and are typically weaker (10–30% of main peak intensity).

For sputtered Mo-Ni-Ox, screening satellites are often weak or absent because:
  • Sputtering can create defects and disorder that suppress screening
  • The sample may be partially reduced (Mo⁰ present), which has no screening
  • Oxide screening satellites are typically only prominent in well-crystallised, stoichiometric oxides

      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"># Screening & Unscreening in Mo 3d Spectra</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">Good question. Let me clarify what you're observing:</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">## What Are Screened vs. Unscreened Peaks?</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">In **transition metal oxides**, particularly Mo 3d, you can have:</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">"• **Unscreened (main) peaks** — the primary 3d photohole is not screened by valence electrons. These are the dominant features and represent the "</text>
      <symbol textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">34</symbol>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">true</text>
      <symbol textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">34</symbol>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">" oxidation state."</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">• **Screened peaks** — the 3d photohole is screened by a valence electron (e.g., 3d⁵L̄ configuration, where L̄ is a ligand hole). These appear at **lower binding energy** (~1–3 eV below the main peak) and are typically **weaker** (10–30% of main peak intensity).</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">## Your Current Fit (8 peaks)</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">Your fit shows **4 oxidation states** (Mo⁰, MoO₂, Mo⁵⁺, MoO₃), each with a 3d5/2 and 3d3/2 doublet. This is a **main-peak-only model** — no screening satellites are included.</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">**Is this correct for your sample?**</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">For **sputtered Mo-Ni-Ox**, screening satellites are often **weak or absent** because:</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">- Sputtering can create defects and disorder that suppress screening</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">- The sample may be partially reduced (Mo⁰ present), which has no screening</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">- Oxide screening satellites are typically only prominent in well-crystallised, stoichiometric oxides</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">## Should You Add Screening Satellites?</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas"></text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">**Check your raw spectrum:**</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">- Look for **small shoulders or bumps 1–3 eV below each main peak** (lower BE side)</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">- If present and visible above noise, add screened components</text>
    </paragraph>
    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">- If absent or negligible, your current 8-peak model is appropriate</text>

      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">• **MoO₂ screened** — ~1–2 eV below MoO₂ main</text>

      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">• **Mo⁵⁺ screened** — ~1–2 eV below Mo⁵⁺ main</text>

    <paragraph>
      <text textcolor="#000000" fontpointsize="9" fontstyle="90" fontweight="400" fontface="Consolas">• **MoO₃ screened** — ~1–2 eV below MoO₃ main (most prominent screening in fully oxidised state)</text>

# Mo 3d Core Level Analysis

The Mo 3d core level was deconvoluted using four spin-orbit split doublets (Mo⁰, Mo⁴⁺, Mo⁵⁺, and Mo⁶⁺) fitted with Gaussian-Lorentzian line shapes against an active Shirley background over the binding energy range 222.08–239.28 eV. Each doublet was constrained with a fixed spin-orbit splitting of 3.1 ± 0.2 eV between the 3d₅/₂ and 3d₃/₂ components, and the 3d₃/₂ peak areas were fixed at 0.667 times their corresponding 3d₅/₂ values to maintain the correct 3:2 intensity ratio. The Mo⁰ species appeared at 227.66 eV (3d₅/₂), while higher oxidation states were observed at 228.44 eV (Mo⁴⁺), 229.99 eV (Mo⁵⁺), and 232.26 eV (Mo⁶⁺), with FWHM values increasing progressively from 0.71 eV for metallic Mo to 2.13 eV for Mo⁵⁺, reflecting increasing disorder in higher oxidation states. The Mo⁶⁺ doublet exhibited a higher Lorentzian character (L/G = 45) compared to other species (L/G = 19), suggesting distinct electronic properties. Peak area analysis revealed substantial contributions from both Mo⁶⁺ (6400 + 4215 = 10615 a.u., ~41% of total) and Mo⁵⁺ (3627 + 2440 = 6067 a.u., ~24%), alongside significant Mo⁴⁺ (3719 + 2520 = 6239 a.u., ~24%) and minor Mo⁰ (5343 + 3617 = 8960 a.u., ~35%) contributions, indicating a mixed-valence molybdenum oxide system with predominant hexavalent character consistent with MoO₃ or partially reduced molybdenum oxide phases.
